dura_en_DU01: The spinal cord and nerve roots are surrounded by a tough membrane. Inside it is a clear fluid that bathes the nerves.
dura_en_DU02: Sometimes this membrane tears during spine surgery. This is a known complication, especially in repeat operations and when the canal is severely narrowed. Usually the surgeon stitches or seals the tear straight away.
dura_en_DU03: If fluid keeps leaking through the tear, the pressure around the brain drops. This can cause a particular kind of headache. In most cases, once repaired, everything heals without lasting effects.
dura_en_DU04: After a tear, the routine varies. Some patients may get up at the usual time; others are told to lie flat for a while. Once the tear is closed, studies have not shown a convincing benefit of prolonged bed rest over getting up early. But it depends on the situation, so the surgeon decides. Follow your surgeon's instructions.
dura_en_DU05: While lying down, move your feet, do breathing exercises and drink if you are allowed. If clot prevention has been prescribed, do not miss it. Sit or stand up only when allowed, and only with the staff.
dura_en_DU06: Tell the staff if you get a headache that gets worse when sitting or standing and eases when lying down. It may come with nausea, neck pain or ringing in the ears. This can be a sign of a fluid leak.
dura_en_DU07: Tell the staff straight away if your dressing gets wet with clear, watery fluid, if such fluid appears in the drain container, or if a soft swelling appears under the wound. Clear discharge does not always mean a leak, but it must be checked.
dura_en_DU08: Try not to strain. If you are constipated, say so; you may be given a laxative. Do not lift anything heavy until the surgeon allows it.
dura_en_DU09: Tell the medical team immediately if the headache is very severe, or you develop a fever, neck pain and stiffness, sensitivity to light, or confusion. dura_en_DU10: If these signs appear at home, go to the emergency department immediately. If there is confusion, new marked weakness, loss of bladder or bowel control, or another serious condition, call one zero one. Do not drive yourself.

stage_ru_ST02: При сильном отёке или повреждённой коже большая операция сразу может повысить риск осложнений со стороны раны. Поэтому иногда лечение проводят в два этапа. stage_ru_ST05: Когда ткани готовы, раму могут заменить внутренней конструкцией: пластиной с винтами или стержнем внутри кости. Иногда наружный фиксатор оставляют до сращения — это тоже окончательный способ лечения.

stage_en_ST01: In a comminuted fracture, the bone is broken into three or more pieces. In a severe injury, the surrounding tissues can also be badly damaged, with major swelling and blisters on the skin. If the fracture connects to the outside through a wound, it is called an open fracture.
stage_en_ST02: With severe swelling or damaged skin, a major operation straight away can increase the risk of wound complications. So treatment is sometimes done in two stages. The surgeon decides. stage_en_ST03: First, an external fixator is applied: a metal frame outside the limb. It is connected to the bone by pins that pass through the skin above and below the fracture, and it holds the bone in the right position.
stage_en_ST04: While the frame holds the bone, the limb is kept raised, and the staff watch the skin and swelling. The surgeon decides how long to wait: until the swelling goes down and the skin is ready.
stage_en_ST05: When the tissues are ready, the frame may be replaced with internal fixation: a plate with screws or a nail inside the bone. Sometimes the external fixator stays until the bone heals, and that is also a final treatment.
stage_en_ST06: The staff regularly check the colour and warmth of your toes, feeling and movement. Tell the staff immediately if you have unusually severe or rapidly increasing pain, a feeling of tightness in the lower leg, new numbness or tingling in the foot, or toes that become cold, pale or bluish. Do not wait until painkillers stop working.
stage_en_ST07: The places where the pins enter the skin need special attention: infection can travel through them deep down, to the bone. Before discharge, the staff will show you how to care for them. Do not touch them with unclean hands, and do not put anything on them unless prescribed.
stage_en_ST08: See a doctor the same day if redness, pain or swelling around a pin increases, or if there is pus or a fever. If a pin feels loose, tell the medical team straight away.
stage_en_ST09: Do not tighten or turn the frame's clamps yourself. Do not lift your leg by the frame unless you have been taught how. Put weight on the leg only as the surgeon allows.
stage_en_ST10: Stopping smoking and eating well create better conditions for bone healing. Take medicines as prescribed. If the doctor prescribes clot prevention, follow the plan, including injections if needed.
stage_en_ST11: If you suddenly feel short of breath or have chest pain, call the staff at once. If you are at home, call one zero one.
stage_en_ST12: This is general advice. Individual instructions from your doctor and medical team come first.

achil_en_AC01: The Achilles tendon connects two calf muscles, the gastrocnemius and soleus, to the heel bone. It lets us stand on tiptoe, walk and run.
achil_en_AC02: A rupture often happens during a sudden push-off or a jump. It can feel as if someone kicked you in the back of the lower leg, sometimes closer to the heel. Sometimes there is a snap, and it is hard to stand on tiptoe.
achil_en_AC03: During the operation, the surgeon stitches the ends of the tendon together. Sometimes a rupture is treated without surgery, in a cast or a boot. The treatment is chosen together with the surgeon.
achil_en_AC04: After surgery, the foot is held in a splint or boot, usually with the toes pointing down. This keeps the repair from stretching. Do not remove the splint or boot or change the position of your foot without permission and instructions from the medical team.
achil_en_AC05: Put weight on the leg only as the surgeon allows. Crutches or a walker are usually used. Following the doctor's plan, the foot is gradually brought back towards its normal position. If the boot has wedges under the heel, they are removed on a set schedule. Do not do this yourself.
achil_en_AC06: For the first few days, keep your leg raised when sitting or lying down. Wiggle your toes if this is allowed.
achil_en_AC07: Keep the dressing clean and dry. After this operation, wound healing problems can occur, so the wound needs to be watched carefully. Do not get it wet, and do not remove the dressing unless told to.
achil_en_AC08: See a doctor the same day if the dressing gets soaked, redness of the wound increases, or there is discharge or a fever. If there is severe pain or pressure under the boot, new numbness, or cold or pale toes, get medical help immediately.
achil_en_AC09: When the leg is immobilised, the risk of blood clots goes up. If prevention has been prescribed, do not miss it. Report pain, swelling or redness in the calf urgently. If you suddenly feel short of breath or have chest pain, call the staff at once; at home, call one zero one.
achil_en_AC10: Do not stand on tiptoe or make sudden movements until you are allowed. If you suddenly feel a new snap or a blow to the back of the lower leg, or notice sudden weakness of the foot, stop putting weight on it and contact your surgeon urgently.
achil_en_AC11: Recovery takes months. A physiotherapist chooses your exercises. Do not smoke: smoking slows healing.

opday_en_OD01: On the day of your operation, we will explain what to expect, from the morning on the ward until your return after surgery.
opday_en_OD02: Follow the instructions you have been given about fasting, drinking and taking medicines. Some medicines are taken on the morning of surgery with a small sip of water. Your doctor or anaesthetist will tell you which ones.
opday_en_OD03: Shower at the time instructed, using the product specified by the ward. Before going to theatre, put on a hospital gown and remove your jewellery and watch. Keep your identification wristband on.
opday_en_OD04: Remove contact lenses, removable dentures and hearing aids according to staff instructions. You may be allowed to keep some of them until you meet the anaesthetist.
opday_en_OD05: When the theatre team is ready, staff will take you to the operating theatre area on a bed or trolley. The nurse will hand over the necessary information to the receiving team.
opday_en_OD06: Before surgery, staff will confirm your name, the planned procedure, the correct side or site, and any allergies. Repeated questions are a normal part of the safety checks.
opday_en_OD07: Your relatives can ask staff where they may wait. Some hospitals have a relatives' waiting area and a screen showing the stages of surgery using a patient number. Ask staff what arrangements are available here.
opday_en_OD08: After surgery, you will usually spend some time in the recovery room under the supervision of medical staff.
opday_en_OD09: When your condition allows, you will be transferred back to the ward. Sometimes additional monitoring or treatment in another unit is needed. The length of your stay depends on the operation, anaesthesia and your condition.
opday_en_OD10: This is general information. Individual instructions from your treating doctor and the medical team responsible for your care take priority.

opday_ar_OD02: التزموا بالتعليمات التي تلقيتموها بشأن الصيام والشرب وتناول الأدوية. يمكن تناول بعض الأدوية صباح العملية مع رشفة صغيرة من الماء. سيخبركم الطبيب المعالج أو طبيب التخدير بالأدوية التي يجب تناولها.
opday_ar_OD03: استحمّوا في الوقت المحدّد وباستخدام المستحضر الذي أوصى به طاقم القسم. قبل الانتقال إلى قسم العمليات، ارتدوا ثوب المستشفى وانزعوا المجوهرات والساعة. لا تنزعوا سوار التعريف.
opday_ar_OD04: انزعوا العدسات اللاصقة وأطقم الأسنان المتحركة وأجهزة السمع وفق تعليمات الطاقم. قد يُسمح لكم بالإبقاء على بعضها حتى مقابلة طبيب التخدير.
opday_ar_OD05: عندما يكون فريق العمليات جاهزًا، سينقلكم الطاقم إلى قسم العمليات على السرير أو على نقالة. وستنقل الممرضة المعلومات الطبية اللازمة إلى الفريق الذي يستقبلكم.
opday_ar_OD06: قبل العملية، سيتأكد الطاقم معكم مرة أخرى من اسمكم ونوع العملية والجهة أو موضع الجراحة، ومن وجود أي حساسية. تكرار هذه الأسئلة جزء طبيعي من إجراءات السلامة.
opday_ar_OD07: يمكن لأفراد عائلتكم سؤال الطاقم عن المكان المسموح لهم بالانتظار فيه. في بعض المستشفيات توجد منطقة انتظار وشاشة تعرض مراحل العملية باستخدام رقم المريض. اسألوا الطاقم عن النظام المتّبع هنا.
opday_ar_OD08: بعد العملية، ستبقون عادةً لبعض الوقت في غرفة الإفاقة تحت مراقبة الطاقم الطبي.
opday_ar_OD09: عندما تسمح حالتكم، ستُنقلون إلى القسم. أحيانًا قد تحتاجون إلى مراقبة إضافية أو علاج في وحدة أخرى. تعتمد مدة البقاء على نوع العملية والتخدير وحالتكم الصحية.
opday_ar_OD10: هذه معلومات عامة. تعليمات طبيبكم المعالج والطاقم الطبي المسؤول عن رعايتكم لها الأولوية على المعلومات العامة.
